title: Ayer
goal: Say what you did yesterday and last week with the preterite of regular verbs.

lessons.title: Yesterday I worked
lessons.notes:
The **preterite** (pretérito) tells finished actions in the past: what you did yesterday, last week, in 2019. For **-ar** verbs, drop -ar and add:
**yo** hablé · **tú** hablaste · **él / ella / usted** habló · **nosotros** hablamos · **ellos / ustedes** hablaron
The accents matter: **hablo** = I speak, **habló** = he spoke. Say the stress where the accent is.
**hablamos** is both "we speak" and "we spoke": the time word tells you which - **ayer hablamos** (we spoke yesterday).
Reflexives work the same: **me levanté**, **se duchó**.

sentences.en: Yesterday I spoke with my mother.
accept_en: Yesterday I talked to my mother.
I spoke to my mother yesterday.
I talked with my mum yesterday.

sentences.en: Did you speak with Carlos last night?
accept_en: Did you talk to Carlos last night?
Did you speak to Carlos last night?

sentences.en: Ana spoke with her dad.
Last night we talked a lot.
accept_en: We talked a lot last night.
Last night we spoke a lot.

sentences.en: My parents spoke with Ana.
Yesterday I worked ten hours.
I got up at seven.
Last night we cooked pasta at home.
accept_en: We cooked pasta at home last night.

sentences.es: Mis amigos bailaron toda la noche.
sentences.en: My friends danced all night.
accept_en: My friends danced all night long.

sentences.en: Did you cook dinner?
accept_en: Was it you who cooked dinner?

sentences.es: Mi hermano se duchó y se acostó.
sentences.en: My brother had a shower and went to bed.
accept_en: My brother showered and went to bed.

lessons.title: Yesterday I ate
lessons.notes:
**-er** and **-ir** verbs share one set of preterite endings:
**yo** comí · **tú** comiste · **él / ella / usted** comió · **nosotros** comimos · **ellos / ustedes** comieron
**yo** viví · **tú** viviste · **él** vivió · **nosotros** vivimos · **ellos** vivieron
Again the accent on the last syllable is the past: **como** (I eat) vs **comió** (he ate).
Stem changes in the present (**vuelvo**, **entiendo**) disappear here: **volví** (I came back), **entendí** (I understood). That makes the preterite easier than it looks.

sentences.es: Ayer comí en un restaurante mexicano.
sentences.en: Yesterday I ate at a Mexican restaurant.
accept_en: I ate at a Mexican restaurant yesterday.
Yesterday I had lunch at a Mexican restaurant.

sentences.en: What did you eat last night?

sentences.es: Sofía comió mucho en el restaurante.
sentences.en: Sofía ate a lot at the restaurant.
Last night I went out with my friends.
accept_en: I went out with my friends last night.

sentences.en: I came back home very late.
accept_en: I went back home very late.

sentences.en: I didn't understand the question.
My grandparents lived in Chile.

sentences.es: Le escribí un mensaje a Pedro.
sentences.en: I wrote Pedro a message.
accept_en: I wrote a message to Pedro.

sentences.es: Los niños comieron y salieron al parque.
sentences.en: The children ate and went out to the park.
accept_en: The kids ate and went out to the park.

lessons.title: Last week
lessons.notes:
Time words that go with the preterite - they mark a finished moment:
**ayer** · **anteayer** (the day before yesterday) · **anoche**
**la semana pasada** · **el mes pasado** · **el año pasado** · **el sábado pasado**
**pasado / pasada** agrees with the noun.
**hace** + time = **ago**, and it goes in front: **hace dos días** (two days ago), **hace un año** (a year ago).
**una vez** = once, **dos veces** = twice.
All of these usually go at the start or the end: **La semana pasada compré un carro.**

sentences.es: La semana pasada visité a mi abuela.
sentences.en: Last week I visited my grandmother.
accept_en: I visited my grandmother last week.
Last week I visited my grandma.

sentences.es: El mes pasado compré una computadora.
sentences.en: Last month I bought a computer.
accept_en: I bought a computer last month.

sentences.es: El año pasado viajamos a Perú.
sentences.en: Last year we travelled to Peru.
accept_en: Last year we traveled to Peru.
We travelled to Peru last year.
Last year we went to Peru.

sentences.en: The day before yesterday I finished the book.
accept_en: I finished the book the day before yesterday.

sentences.es: Hablé con ella hace dos días.
sentences.en: I spoke with her two days ago.
accept_en: I talked to her two days ago.
I spoke to her two days ago.

sentences.es: Hace un año viví en México.
sentences.en: A year ago I lived in Mexico.
accept_en: I lived in Mexico a year ago.

sentences.es: El sábado pasado salimos a bailar.
sentences.en: Last Saturday we went out dancing.
accept_en: We went out dancing last Saturday.
Last Saturday we went out to dance.

sentences.en: I visited the museum once.
accept_en: I went to the museum once.

sentences.en: Did you finish the work yesterday?
accept_en: Did you finish the job yesterday?

lessons.title: Spelling changes
lessons.notes:
A few verbs change their spelling in the **yo** form only, to keep the sound:
**llegar** -> **llegué** (keeps the hard g) · **jugar** -> **jugué** · **pagar** -> **pagué**
**buscar** -> **busqué** (keeps the k sound) · **tocar** -> **toqué**
**empezar** -> **empecé** (z becomes c before e)
The other persons are regular: **llegaste, llegó, llegamos, llegaron**.
Verbs like **leer** put a **y** between vowels: **leyó**, **leyeron** (and **leíste** with an accent).
**empezar** changes e -> ie in the present (**empiezo**) but not in the preterite.

sentences.es: Llegué al trabajo a las nueve.
sentences.en: I arrived at work at nine.
accept_en: I got to work at nine.

sentences.en: What time did you arrive last night?
accept_en: What time did you get home last night?
What time did you get in last night?

sentences.es: El sábado jugué al fútbol con mi hijo.
sentences.en: On Saturday I played football with my son.
accept_en: On Saturday I played soccer with my son.
I played football with my son on Saturday.

sentences.en: I paid for dinner by card.
accept_en: I paid for the dinner by card.
I paid for dinner with a card.

sentences.es: Busqué mis llaves toda la mañana.
sentences.en: I looked for my keys all morning.
accept_en: I searched for my keys all morning.

sentences.es: Empecé a estudiar español el año pasado.
sentences.en: I started studying Spanish last year.
accept_en: I started to study Spanish last year.
I began studying Spanish last year.
Last year I started learning Spanish.

sentences.en: My dad read your message.

sentences.es: Los niños leyeron un libro en la biblioteca.
sentences.en: The children read a book in the library.
accept_en: The kids read a book in the library.
The children read a book at the library.

sentences.es: La película empieza a las ocho.
sentences.en: The film starts at eight.
What did you look for in the shop?
accept_en: What were you looking for in the shop?
What did you look for in the store?
